Q01.text: All three entry points call require_activation first; the disabled path returns before any host, config or helper side effect. The enabled path requires a bounded regular approval file, strict JSON (duplicate keys and non-finite values refused), exact FIELDS, schema, scope and execute_once; actuation and model qualification False; exact capture/operation ids, GPU, ROOT, PYTHON, the lock flag and a 40-hex preregistration commit; digests of SHA256SUMS, PROTOCOL, NATIVE_PLAN and OFFERS; exactly four acceptances with per-kind subjects and hashed receipt bytes; and a hashed fresh-host receipt. These are filesystem attestations, not cryptography. MAYOR_APPROVAL_TEMPLATE_INVALID.json fails at authorization02.py:53-57 (execute_once false; also lock flag false, null commit/manifest/receipts, accepted false).

Q02.text: The approval binds the deployment SHA256SUMS, PROTOCOL, NATIVE_PLAN and OFFERS digests, CONSUMER_SEAL (successor01 manifest 13bc7f83...), ids, GPU, ROOT and PYTHON. CONSUMER_SEAL is the reviewed-successor identity: it is also bound by the receipts' successor subjects, invocation_check, the invocation file and the SUCCESSOR-SHA256SUMS copy check. The runnable consumer is the deployment copy, bound by the deployment manifest digest (approval), the consumer CONTROL_FREEZE (runtime; READY 104; launcher registration 84; SOURCE_BINDING 77-80) and the top-level CONTROL_FREEZE. Hash-only identity: consumer01, worker01, validate01, generation01, ipc01 and fixture01 equal successor01; common01 (NAMESPACE/CAPTURE), seal_inputs01 (delegates to ../pins02.py), NATIVE_PLAN/OFFERS (ids) and CONTROL_FREEZE changed as declared in EXACT_SOURCE_DIFF.patch. Python: remote_only requires HERE==STAGE, sys.prefix==PYTHON venv, isolated, dont_write_bytecode, no optimize; children run c.PYTHON -I -B and the worker sys.executable -I -B.

Q03.text: Order: gate, remote_only, verify_code, namespace, lock, mkdir, startup alarm, fresh host, prerequisites, config, Owned, native, gateway, invocation, client, monitor. Refusals: disabled, missing approval, template, any binding mismatch, spent namespace, lock contention (before namespace creation), fresh-host mismatch (after namespace creation, N01), relative receipt paths in children (N03), cancelled or late before a service or the client. A READY/registration failure is fail-closed but lacks a machine-readable class (N04). Popen-to-registration: the worker is a client main-thread child discovered by the 50 ms remember(), then pinned by register_leaf with pidfd; residual windows N11 and N12 remain premises.

Q04.text: A single activation (client01.py:618-622) sets active_at, the deadline active+20 and active-start.json; the consumer lease uses authority.start(active_at+20) (consumer01.py:177), so the active end is shared. The pipeline min(begin+.080, source+.500, active end) is computed in consumer code byte-identical to successor01 (PIPELINE .080 unchanged at consumer/common01.py:22); this review inherits it from scr01 under A01-A12 and does not re-derive it. Producer cuts use min(deadline, now+.5) at 500, 599 and 631, as in base acquire01 451/524. A consumer-only refusal is caught at 494-496 or 520-521, the producer cut proceeds, and the deadline is not reset; consumer01.py:171-175 forbid a second begin or a non-ordinal-2 substitute, and there is no retry. Source clock: markers, invocation and anchors are bound to c.domain() (boot id plus time namespace).

Q05.text: Unchanged against base acquire01: settings .2 s/1900/1 MiB (client01 33 = base 31); warmup limit 60 (249 = 226); managed limit 20 (469 = 427); CAS not_after +.5 (292 = 267); final deadline (655 = 573). Capture requires maximum_http_exchanges <= 1900 (transport01.py:20-21). The .2 s value is the per-exchange HTTP timeout, not an inference cap; inference uses limit=60 for warmup and 20 for managed, as in the base. bounded_loop waits only tighten toward the cutoff (823-825).

Q06.text: Offers start as not_sent and change fate only on observed transport; all_offered uses the reported offers, or unobserved/not_sent when no result exists, requires exactly the two planned request_ids, lists raw receipts, the warmup-send flag and missing_receipt_not_proof_of_no_send. Consumer publication refusals are retained. No relabelling was found. Gap: on any non-joined path (including D2-F1) all-offered.json is never written (316 before 317); N06 can lose a begin-refusal reason.

Q07.text: publish converts any exception into invalidate_publication: sticky authority poison, a refusal row (consumer_refused_producer_continues; counted=False unless an attempt row exists, then counted=committed), errors, a refusal file and cleanup component_pass False. Capture.observed routes publisher exceptions to the same invalidator and requires authority_poisoned on refusal receipts. The client wrapper ignores the return value (357-359), but refusals are sticky and enforced at client01.py:675-677, consumer01.py:419-420/435 and launch01.py:337, so an ignored return never means an absent refusal (R-ATTR). counted=False is not proof that nothing was written (R-COUNT). R-SR4: consumer and transport files are byte-identical; no Gateway strictness was added; strict duplicate-key refusal remains a Native-only claim.

Q08.text: Normal order: protocol-finished, launcher anchor, cleanup arm, owned.cleanup (natural phase until min(anchor+7, deadline-33); services signalled after the client exits; scoped reap 30; join 2; reserve 1). In parallel the client reads the shared anchor, closes the wire, and awaits boundary.close(). The consumer writes a pre-return component.json (status cleanup_evidence_pending_final_return_guard, component_pass False) and returns status complete with cleanup_return_guard_at. The client writes consumer-close-returned02.json (0600) only after the return. persist_close requires joined and a private single-link file, copies the bytes exclusively with fsync, and checks schema, domain, anchor, cutoff, deadline, status complete, all_joined and chronology. The pre-return component.json cannot substitute. Shared teardown ownership is broken only on the D2-F1 paths.

Q09.text: The config is created only after all prerequisites; the key is redacted at capture (Reader, Capture.scrub) and in failures. Export order: supervision.json; if joined, scan -> result-index -> rescan -> close_private_config (joined, scan, safe-export proof, key identity, unlink, record) -> rescan; then export-gate (safe and removed). Response bodies stored as response_body_base64 are decoded by the scan. On a non-joined path (D2-F1) the config is retained and export is refused.

Q10.text: PROTOCOL bounds 260/180/20/3/40/17 equal the base. Startup alarm started+180; monitor deadline active+23 or started+180 with cap started+203; cleanup bound min(anchor+40, started+243); IO deadline min(started+260, cleanup_finished+17); phase_bounds 344-347; consumer activation requires active+20+3+40+17 <= hard deadline; invocation_check requires exact +180/+260/+243. Teardown allocation 7/30/2/1 = 40. No bound is broadened.

Q11.text: See r_rules_applicability: claim limits for the model-free diagnostic; blocking for a formal paired study.

launch01.py:294-308: main's outer finally (294-360) starts with lines 295-296 outside any inner try (as are 309-313); an exception there leaves main and skips 349-360. The inner try publishes host-cleanup-anchor02.json first (298-299; composition_common01.py:54-61 exclusive partial open, dump, fsync, rename), re-arms for cleanup (300), and only then calls owned.cleanup (301-303); except BaseException (307-308) records 'cleanup:<type>' and leaves cleanup=None.

owned01.py:66-83: owned roots are spawned with start_new_session=True and without a parent-death signal; the subreaper role exists only in the launcher process (owned01.py:59-64; source13-entry02.py:71-80); service01.py:84-103 execs Native/Gateway inside the owned root processes.
effects: Native vLLM, Gateway, client and consumer worker keep running in their own sessions after the launcher exits; no owned process group is signalled. Descendant PID/start-tick identities exist only in launcher memory (owned.identities) and are lost; on disk remain each root's started.json (pid, start_ticks, process_group) and consumer-registered02.json.

The flock on c.LOCK is released at 358-360 (or at process exit in the 295-296 sub-case) while owned GPU processes may still run. A later launch of this design would refuse at its own idle/fresh-host checks (launch01.py:246, 261), but any other user of the lock must rely on its own idle check.
all-offered.json is not written. client/result.json and client/http receipts remain on disk if the client finished, but the launcher-level all-offered summary is missing.
The private config holding ADMIN_API_KEY stays in STATE because close_private_config requires joined.

Reporting stays truthful: cleanup=null, owned_joined=false, errors contain 'cleanup:<type>' (or the launcher exits with a TimeoutError traceback), export-gate safe_to_export=false, component_pass=false. No false-pass or relabelling risk was found.

Record the run as a supervision failure, never as a workload outcome; preserve every output.

findings.title: A pending monitor alarm or a failed cleanup-anchor publication skips owned.cleanup, leaving Native, Gateway, client and consumer worker running after the launcher exits and the GPU lock released

triggers.text: After monitor returns normal=True at 95, the timer armed at 102 is still pending for min(started+203, active+23). The client's final phase is bounded by min(active+23, end+3) (client01.py:655), so in the slow/stall regime (active phase ending close to its 20 s bound and the final drain/capture running to its deadline) protocol-finished.json can be observed only tens of milliseconds before active+23. If the alarm is delivered while lines 297-300 run (publish/fsync/rename or arm), TimeoutError is caught at 307 and owned.cleanup is skipped; if it is delivered at 295-296, TimeoutError escapes main's finally and no supervision.json, export-gate.json or all-offered.json is written. The same exposure applies when monitor raises a non-alarm error (for example late_or_inconsistent_protocol_completion, 92-94) shortly before the pending alarm.
triggers.window: about one 50 ms poll plus the anchor publish/fsync duration, immediately before active+23; narrow but correlated with the busy regime this diagnostic is meant to observe

triggers.text: Any OSError from c.publish at 298-299 (open, write, fsync or rename: ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EIO) or from the c.domain() procfs reads is caught at 307 and owned.cleanup is skipped. (exclusive_marker is not a realistic cause: only the launcher publishes this file, once; client01.py:722 and 813 only read it.)

If the pending alarm is delivered inside the except body (291-293) before supervision is reassigned, supervision keeps its initial anchor=started (244); arm(min(started+40, started+243)) at 300 then raises phase_deadline_already_exhausted whenever more than 40 s have elapsed since started, so owned.cleanup is skipped and the TimeoutError propagates after the finally completes.

notes.recommendation: Mayor validates the fresh-host receipt immediately before launch.
notes.text: fresh_host runs after the one-attempt namespace and the lock (225-231). A stale (>3600 s) or mismatching receipt refuses only after STATE/PUBLIC exist, which spends the single attempt. fresh_host reloads the receipt by path after authorization02 hashed it (no re-hash; trusted-filesystem premise).

notes.recommendation: Prereg cites four distinct receipt files, one per decision.
notes.text: Exactly four acceptance kinds are required, each with accepted True, its own subject (successor_* -> CONSUMER_SEAL, observational_* -> protocol sha, deployment -> manifest sha) and a regular, single-link, <=16 MiB receipt whose bytes hash to the declared sha. Receipt contents are never parsed, and paths/digests are not required to be pairwise distinct: both successor_* kinds share one subject, so one file could satisfy both. Separation of the four Mayor decisions is therefore a trusted-Mayor procedural premise. lstat-then-read is a TOCTOU window under the trusted-filesystem premise.

notes.recommendation: Prereg requires absolute receipt and fresh-host paths.
notes.text: Only the approval path is made absolute (89). Receipt and fresh-host paths are used as given: services re-validate with cwd=HERE and the client with cwd=PREFLIGHT, so a relative path that resolves in the launcher's cwd fails closed in a child after namespace, config and service startup.

notes.recommendation: Prereg analysis rule: client-session-refused.json present and active-start.json absent means startup prerequisite/supervision failure, never a workload outcome.
notes.text: A READY or registration failure writes client-session-refused.json, and shared_teardown_anchor then publishes protocol-finished.json with reason client_startup_or_protocol_refusal; the monitor returns normal=True and the launcher records only 'postflight:FileNotFoundError' (result.json absent). The outcome is fail-closed and all_offered labels both offers unobserved, but no machine-readable startup_prerequisite_failure class exists, and the reason string merges startup and protocol refusal.

If the launcher's cleanup anchor differs from the client's (abnormal launcher return between the client's two anchor reads), HostBoundConsumer.close refuses one_shared_cleanup_anchor before the consumer's own close; the leaf is left to the launcher reap and no RETURNED receipt exists.

notes.recommendation: Retain begin and cut refusals in separate fields in any successor.
notes.text: A begin refusal stored in attempt['consumer'] (495) is overwritten by a later cut refusal (528). begin raises without appending to the consumer's errors, so the begin reason can be lost when both begin and the cut refuse. handoff-intent.json survives unless the refusal precedes consumer01.py:173 (client01.py:492 or consumer01.py:171). Fail-closed: no client lease, no handoff.

begin runs synchronously before the producer cut; cut_deadline=min(deadline, now+.5) is computed after begin, so the producer keeps its full .5 s but starts later by the begin duration. The clocks to report this exist (collection_boundary_started_at, collector_call_entered_at, cut_returned_at).

notes.recommendation: Premise P06; optionally decode .jsonl lines in a successor.
notes.text: privacy_scan searches raw bytes of every file and decodes only values under keys ending in '_base64' inside .json files. .jsonl/.log files and other encodings are not decoded, so the export-gate wording 'decoded response bodies' holds only for *_base64 JSON fields. Capture-time redaction (owned01 Reader, transport01.py:31-32, composition_common01.py:294-296) mitigates.

notes.recommendation: Exclude them from the remote stage copy or ignore them in the manifest comparison.
notes.text: The 20 symlinks are not covered by SHA256SUMS; they have no runtime role.

A default-OFF invocation without -B/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE imports stage modules before the gate returns and can create __pycache__ inside the stage; verify_code checks only listed files. The live path enforces dont_write_bytecode through remote_only.

SIGALRM is the only signal whose handler raises. Delivered between Popen returning and roots.append (68-71), or before the identity/pidfd are recorded (72-76), it could leave a spawned root untracked. Spawns happen only before started+180 while the startup alarm targets started+180, so this needs a spawn within the last instants of startup.

remember walks only /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children (children of each process's main thread); remember_adopted exists but owned01 never calls it. The consumer worker is spawned from the client's event-loop main thread, so the 50 ms launcher remember() can discover it before registration. Descendants spawned from non-main threads, or orphans adopted between polls, are not discovered by this walk; cleanup then relies on process-group signalling and on the worker's own EOF/hard-deadline exit.

notes.recommendation: Premise P02: the Mayor verifies the staged copy against the full deployment02 SHA256SUMS on the fresh host.
notes.text: Runtime pins cover INPUTS/INPUT_FREEZE (including the owner helper copy), ADDITIONAL_INPUTS, the SUCCESSOR-SHA256SUMS copy, PLAN/OFFERS copies, SOURCE_BINDING, the consumer CONTROL_FREEZE map and the top-level CONTROL_FREEZE map. consumer/common01.py and seal_inputs01.py are imported and executed before their own digests are checked (self-verification), and the top-level map lists consumer/CONTROL_FREEZE.json but not consumer/*.py. The approval compares the deployment SHA256SUMS digest as a value; the 479-entry manifest is not re-verified at runtime. This detects accidental change, not adversarial change.

notes.recommendation: Prereg defines the field's meaning and makes the launcher the c.LOCK acquirer.
notes.text: acquire_lock takes flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on c.LOCK through a new open file description, before the namespace exists and outside the try. If another Mayor process (for example a flock(1) wrapper) holds that lock, the launcher refuses with BlockingIOError and no side effect. existing_Mayor_exclusive_GPU_lock_held=True therefore cannot mean that another process holds a flock on c.LOCK during the run. The lock fd is non-inheritable, so children never hold it.

premises.text: Trusted Mayor and filesystem: approval and receipts are filesystem attestations checked by byte digest, not cryptographic signatures; receipt contents are not interpreted; no adversarial swaps in lstat/read windows.

The remote stage equals sealed deployment02, checked against the full SHA256SUMS on the fresh host; the interpreter is c.PYTHON; the launcher runs isolated and without bytecode writing (remote_only enforces both).

OS ownership: start_new_session process groups contain all Native/Gateway descendants, or process-group signalling covers descendants the children walk misses; PID plus start-tick identity and pidfd semantics hold.
The consumer worker exits on pipe EOF or at its hard deadline when the launcher reap does not reach it (scr01 A-series, Mayor-accepted at 93221982741a723c17ecdc3732baec16a42829c6).
No other GPU user ignores c.LOCK or the Mayor's exclusive-GPU procedure.
No component writes the admin key in an encoding the privacy scan does not decode.
Consumer runtime files byte-identical to successor01 (consumer01, worker01, validate01, generation01, ipc01, fixture01) carry the scr01 conclusions only under conditional A01-A12.
Binding completeness relies on the Mayor Parent inventory (128+1 bindings, c00d29d2296bda7e249578f2de7c08650a4d79c9), which this review did not re-derive.

questions.Q01: Approval: pure default-OFF validation before any host, config or helper side effect; four separate Mayor receipts, each bound to its own scope and subject, plus fresh-host and preregistration requirements (trusted filesystem attestations, not cryptographic); the invalid template is refused.
questions.Q02: Bindings: exact deployment, protocol, plan, offers, successor and Python bindings; identity and CONSUMER_SEAL rebinding; interpreter manifest consistency.
questions.Q03: Launch order: launcher, then the two services, then the client; denied paths; mandatory READY/registration failures; ownership gaps between Popen and registration.
questions.Q04: Deadlines: consumer pipeline min(begin+.080, source+.500, original active end) and the source clock; producer collection min(call+.5, original active end); a consumer-only refusal must not reset producer deadlines, substitute the ordinal or retry.
questions.Q05: Transport budgets: .2 acquisition and global 1900 unchanged; inference 60 / remaining 20 exceptions; acquisition .2 is not an inference cap.
questions.Q06: Fates: every offered, not-sent, unknown, failed and cleanup outcome is retained, with no relabelling.
questions.Q07: Poison and publication failure behavior; R-ATTR (an ignored return must not mean an absent refusal), R-COUNT (counted=false is not proof of no write), R-SR4 (gateway strictness).
questions.Q08: Cleanup order, the real RETURNED receipt versus a pre-return component.json, and shared teardown ownership.
questions.Q09: Config, privacy and Base64 export safety.
questions.Q10: Original budgets 260/180/20/3/40/17 are respected and not broadened.
questions.Q11: Whether R-SR4, R-ATTR and R-COUNT apply to the model-free diagnostic versus a formal paired study.

R_ATTR.diagnostic: report begin, producer cut, handoff and publication durations separately from the existing clocks; no arm attribution; begin-before-cut ordering disclosed (N07)
R_ATTR.formal_paired_study: blocking until prospective identical-infrastructure and attribution rules exist

R_COUNT.diagnostic: counted=False is not proof of no write; publication cost and busy incidence count all attempt rows (committed or not) and every sticky refusal
R_COUNT.formal_paired_study: blocking for count/cost metrics until write-ahead attempt accounting is defined

R_SR4.diagnostic: claim_limit_only: strict duplicate-key refusal is Native-only; deployment02 adds no Gateway strictness (consumer and transport files byte-identical)
R_SR4.formal_paired_study: blocking unless both arms share an identical parser path or Gateway strictness is added and independently reviewed

r_rules_applicability.scope: A model-free component run measures publication cost, busy incidence, producer continuation and whole-boundary timing; it is not a paired study and supports no arm-versus-arm attribution.

remaining_live_conditions: D2-F1 resolved by R-a (surgical successor plus a focused control) or R-b (explicit Mayor risk acceptance plus a preregistered manual reap/GPU-idle procedure) before the single live attempt.
Four distinct Mayor receipt files with absolute paths (N02, N03), fresh-host receipt validated immediately before launch (N01), and the preregistration commit.
Full staged-copy verification against deployment02 SHA256SUMS on the fresh host; launch isolated with -B (N13, P02).
Lock-field semantics defined; the launcher is the c.LOCK acquirer (N14).
Preregistered analysis rules: startup-prerequisite classification (N04), begin-refusal retention (N06), R-ATTR durations (N07), R-COUNT all-attempt cost, R-SR4 claim limit, and no paired-study claim.
Premises P01-P08 accepted by the Mayor, or tested separately.
Separate Mayor acceptance of this deployment and the Mayor's freeze/prereg; this review grants nothing.
